evals.name: add-required-property
evals.prompt: `[EventType] public record CustomerRegistered(CustomerId Id, string Name);` has thousands of stored events. Add a required `Country` (string) property that old events should read as 'Unknown'. Write the C# for the records and the migration. Give the code in your reply; do not write files.
evals.expected_output: Current record bumped to [EventType(generation: 2)] with Country, prior record marked [EventTypeGenerationFor<CustomerRegistered>(1)], and an EventTypeMigration<CustomerRegistered, CustomerRegisteredV1> with Upcast using DefaultValue and a declared Downcast.
assertions: Bumps the current record to [EventType(generation: 2)] and adds the Country property.
Keeps the old shape as a separate record marked [EventTypeGenerationFor<CustomerRegistered>(1)] without its own [EventType].
Derives a migration from EventTypeMigration<CustomerRegistered, CustomerRegisteredV1> and uses DefaultValue(target => target.Country, "Unknown") in Upcast.
Declares Downcast too, using IEventMigrationBuilder with the flipped generic order <CustomerRegisteredV1, CustomerRegistered>, even if its Properties lambda is empty.

evals.name: split-and-no-such-methods
evals.prompt: A stored event has `FullName`; the new generation has `FirstName` and `LastName`. A developer tries `properties.Rename(...)` and `properties.Join(...)`. Show the correct upcast and downcast property operations and say what is wrong with those names. Reply with code.
evals.expected_output: Upcast uses Split with PropertySeparator.Space and SplitPartIndex.First/Second; Downcast uses Combine; there is no Rename (RenamedFrom) and no Join (Combine).
assertions: Upcast uses Split with PropertySeparator.Space and SplitPartIndex.First and SplitPartIndex.Second.
Downcast uses Combine with PropertySeparator.Space over the first and last name sources.
States there is no Rename (the method is RenamedFrom) and no Join (concatenation is Combine).

evals.name: enum-change-rules
evals.prompt: For a stored event with an enum property, what happens and what is required for: (a) adding a member, (b) renaming a member, (c) removing a member, (d) renumbering members? Reply only.
evals.expected_output: Chronicle compares enums by underlying values: adding and renaming are compatible; removing and renumbering are incompatible, needing a new generation plus a value map via MapValues, otherwise registration fails with EventTypeSchemaChanged.
assertions: States adding a member is compatible and needs no migration.
States renaming a member is compatible and needs no migration because the underlying values are unchanged.
States removing or renumbering members is incompatible and needs a new generation plus a value map.
States an incompatible change without a new generation fails registration with EventTypeSchemaChanged.

evals.name: greenfield-and-rollout
evals.prompt: A team is two days into a prototype with disposable dev data and wants to write migrations for every event tweak. Another team is about to register a new generation on a multi-silo production kernel. What do you advise each? Reply only.
evals.expected_output: Greenfield with disposable data: rename and change freely, a migration written too early is dead code. Production: registering starts add-only backfill in the default namespace's event log only, and new generations should be registered only after every kernel silo is upgraded.
assertions: Advises the prototype team that migrations are only needed once events of the prior shape exist somewhere that cannot be regenerated, and they can otherwise rename and change freely.
States that registering a new generation starts add-only backfill in the default namespace's event log only.
States new generations should be registered only after every kernel silo is upgraded because an old worker can overwrite content mid-rollout.
